name: Duplicati
summary: Duplicati is an open-source backup tool that encrypts data with AES-256 on the machine before upload and writes to storage the buyer picks, from Amazon S3 and Azure to SFTP and a NAS. Its paid plans add central monitoring: the Free plan watches 2 machines, and Pro and Enterprise start at about $2 and $3 per machine a month.

facts.text: According to the home page, all data is encrypted with AES-256 locally, before it reaches the network and cloud.
The restore guide says Duplicati selects the most recent version by default, and a dropdown lets the user pick a different version to restore from.
On the home page, retention options such as keeping a set number of backups or deleting backups older than a chosen age are listed, and heavy backups can be scheduled for off-peak hours.
Duplicati's home page lists Amazon S3, Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud, Dropbox, OneDrive, Backblaze, IDrive e2, SFTP, WebDAV, external drives and NAS among supported destinations.
On the pricing page, the Pro plan card shows both $2 and $2.50 without saying which applies.

plans.name: Free
plans.notes: Marked always free. Monitors up to 2 machines and shows the last 200 backups.

plans.name: Pro
plans.notes: The card shows both $2 and $2.50 per machine per month on annual billing, so we leave the price unset. Up to 100 machines, 3-year monitoring retention, 100 GB storage per machine.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.notes: Listed as from $3 per machine per month on a yearly contract, minimum 10 machines.

hiddenCosts: Additional storage costs $0.60 per 100 GB per month, billed yearly.
Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace backup add-ons are listed at $0.50 per user per month, billed yearly.
